name: MalletStation
summary: Single-port family. Application reports SysEx product ID LSB 39 (0x27); bootloader re-enumerates under its own distinct product string "malletStation Bootloader".

notes: bootloaderPidMsb follows the standard 0/1 convention by assumption, not confirmed against real hardware or bootloader source (the bootloader ships only as a vendored prebuilt binary; source is unavailable).

The application firmware does not answer a standard Universal Device Inquiry - it reports version only via a proprietary OSC-over-SysEx message. Confirm a successful update by application-mode reconnect (by port name) rather than a version-matched identity reply.
The bootloader erases its whole application region when it recognizes the first firmware packet, blocking USB until that finishes, so chunk 1's reply needs extra grace beyond the steady-state delay.
MalletStation reboots straight into application mode as it commits the final chunk and never answers an identity request on the bootloader port afterwards.
Requests a reboot into bootloader mode while the device still reports as malletStation.
Single monolithic SysEx message (85531 bytes, one F0...F7 pair), not Hex_to_SysEx-chunked. Predates this family's registration in sendsysex; kept for reference/compatibility.
Chunk-safe (-cs512) packaging via Hex_to_SysEx, paired with bootloader v1.0.3.
Distinct product string from the application (unlike K-Board, whose bootloader keeps the app's product string and is disambiguated only by PID MSB) - see identity.notes for MSB caveat.
